title: Adaptive prefix coalescing and TTL hysteresis for bursty workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Produce a deployable playbook, simulator, and safe rollout plan for prefix coalescing + TTL hysteresis that reduces per-token cost for bursty traffic patterns without increasing tail latency or violating latency SLOs. Scope covers: hit-rate modeling for coalesced prefixes, TTL hysteresis heuristics (different up/down time constants), cache-key design guidance to avoid collision amplification, telemetry instrumentation, and staged apply/rollback criteria. This ticket delivers the design doc, a simulator notebook, CI checks for safety gates, and a helm/flag-based staged rollout orchestrator.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator demonstrates >=10% token-cost reduction on 3 representative bursty traces while P95 latency change <= 5ms
Playbook contains explicit hysteresis parameters and safe-apply thresholds for canary, cohort, and global stages
CI includes smoke test that rejects config when hit-rate decreases by >3% vs baseline or error-rate increases >1%
Runbook lists rollback triggers, automations to revert configs, and required postmortem artifacts
technical_notes: Modeling approach: use a two-layer generative model for prefix access patterns: baseline long-tail prefix frequency (Zipf alpha estimated per-customer) + episodic burst process (Poisson arrival of bursts with gamma-distributed sizes). Hit-rate with coalescing computed analytically for simple prefix merges and validated with a Monte Carlo cache simulator. TTL hysteresis: separate parameters for climb (t_up) and decay (t_down) where t_up < t_down to prevent oscillation during burst falloff. Key metrics: effective cache hit-rate, per-request added latency from lookup/merge, KV-memory delta, and downstream GPU token cost. Safe thresholds: require headroom margin (expected hit-rate uplift * 0.6) before global apply. Implementation notes: support flaggable prefix-group definitions, dynamic TTL overrides via runtime policy, and shadow replay to measure impact before apply. Avoid designs that increase key cardinality; recommend canonicalization rules (strip ephemeral IDs, normalize query fields) and a small deterministic hashing step to bound collision risk.
rollout_plan: 1) Local simulation + bench notebook (engineers) 2) Shadow mode on 5% traffic for 48h (observe hit-rate, P50/P95 latency, error rate) 3) Canary cohort (10% traffic) with automated evaluation after 6h and 24h windows 4) Gradual ramp (10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%) with metric gates at each step 5) Global apply with continuous monitoring. Each stage includes automatic rollback if gate violations persist for two consecutive windows. Configs exposed as feature flags and ConfigMap entries for private deployments. All changes go through a one-click rollback automation in Console for Dedicated and Private customers.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: coalescing may create hot keys causing KV-store throttling. Mitigation: enforce per-prefix QPS caps and probe probe-scan to detect hot-key amplification. Risk: oscillation due to rapid on/off bursts. Mitigation: hysteresis with asymmetric t_up/t_down and minimum dwell time before policy changes. Risk: metric noise leading to false rollbacks. Mitigation: use aggregated windows and require sustained violation across two windows. Risk: increased collision from aggressive canonicalization. Mitigation: maintain a collision-backoff policy and sampling-based collision detector to surface high-collision prefixes.
